p.src: Now Baoyu and Baochai, hearing that Xifeng's illness had become critical, rose in haste. The maids attended them with candles. Just as they were about to leave the courtyard, someone sent by Lady Wang arrived and said, “Second Mistress Lian is failing, though she has not yet breathed her last. Second Master and Mistress had better wait a little before going over. There is something strange about Second Mistress Lian's illness. From the third watch until the fourth, she never stopped raving, calling for a boat and a sedan chair and saying that she must return to Jinling and enter the register. No one understood her; she merely wept and cried out. Second Master Lian could think of nothing else to do, so he had a paper boat and sedan chair made. They have not yet been brought in, and Second Mistress Lian is gasping as she waits for them. We were sent to tell you to wait until Second Mistress Lian has passed away before coming over.” “How strange,” said Baoyu. “What does she want to go to Jinling for?” Xiren said softly to Baoyu, “Don't you remember the dream you had that year? I recall you mentioning a number of registers. Wasn't Second Mistress Lian there too?” Baoyu nodded when he heard this. “Yes, indeed. What a pity I no longer remember what was written in them. If so, everyone's fate must be predetermined. But I wonder where Cousin Lin has gone. Now that you have mentioned it, I think I understand a little. If I ever have that dream again, I shall examine everything carefully; then I may gain the power to foresee the future.” Xiren said, “It is quite impossible to talk to someone like you! I make one chance remark, and you immediately take it seriously. Even if you could foresee the future, what could you do about it?” “The trouble is that I cannot,” replied Baoyu. “If I could, I would have no need to worry myself senseless over all of you.”

p.src: While the two were speaking, Baochai came over and asked, “What are you talking about?” Afraid that she would question him closely, Baoyu merely said, “We were talking about Cousin Feng.” Baochai said, “She is on the point of death, yet you still persist in discussing her. Last year you accused me of cursing her, but has not that fortune-stick prediction now come true?” Baoyu thought for a moment, then clapped his hands. “Yes, yes! That would mean you can foresee the future. Then let me ask you outright: do you know what will become of me?” Baochai laughed. “Now you are talking nonsense again. I merely offered a fanciful interpretation of the words on her fortune stick, and you took it seriously. You are just like Cousin Xing. When you lost your jade, she asked Miaoyu to perform planchette divination. No one understood the message that came through, yet afterward she told me in private how Miaoyu could foresee the future and how deeply she had penetrated the Way through meditation. Yet now that this great calamity has befallen Miaoyu, she herself did not know it was coming. Can that be called foreknowledge? Even though my chance remark about Second Mistress has come true, do I really know what has happened to her? I fear I do not even know what will happen to me. Such notions of foretelling what will happen are sheer absurdities. How can they be believed?” “Let us not speak of her,” said Baoyu. Tell me only about Cousin Xing. So many things have happened here one after another that I had completely forgotten about her affair. How could such an important event in your family be concluded so hastily, without even inviting your relatives and friends?” Baochai replied, “There you go being pedantic again. Of all our relatives, only your family here and the Wangs are closely related to us. There is no one of any consequence left in the Wang family. Your family was in mourning after the Old Lady's death, so we did not invite anyone from here either; Second Cousin Lian merely helped make a few arrangements. There were one or two other branches of relatives as well, but since you did not go, how would you know? When one thinks of it, my second sister-in-law's fate is much like mine. She was properly betrothed to my second brother, and Mother had originally intended to give him a splendid wedding. But first, my elder brother was in prison and my second brother was unwilling to make a grand affair of it; second, there were the troubles in your family; and third, my second sister-in-law was suffering terribly under the First Lady, especially after their property was confiscated. The First Lady is rather harsh, and my sister-in-law truly found life unbearable. So I spoke to Mother, and we made do with a modest wedding and brought her into the family. I find that my second sister-in-law is now content and willingly devoted to my mother; she treats her ten times better than a daughter-in-law of her own choosing might have done. She also fulfills every duty of a wife toward my second brother and gets on very well with Xiangling. When my second brother is away, the two of them live together in perfect harmony. Though they are somewhat poor, Mother has lately been rather more at ease. Only when she thinks of my elder brother can she not help grieving.

p.src: Baoyu was still about to explain why he would not move when Lady Wang sent someone to say, “Second Mistress Lian has breathed her last. Everyone else has gone over already. Second Master and Second Mistress are requested to come at once.” At this news, Baoyu could no longer contain himself; he stamped his feet and was about to weep. Baochai too was grief-stricken, but fearing that Baoyu would be overcome with sorrow, she said, “Rather than cry here, we may as well go there and cry.” The two of them then went straight to Xifeng’s quarters. There they saw a great many people gathered around, weeping. Baochai went forward and, seeing that Xifeng had already been laid out upon the deathbed, burst into loud lamentation. Baoyu too took Jia Lian by the hand and began to sob bitterly. Jia Lian began weeping all over again. Ping’er and the others, seeing that no one was offering consolation, had no choice but to suppress their own grief, step forward, and persuade them to stop. Yet everyone continued to grieve without cease. Jia Lian was now utterly at a loss. He sent for Lai Da and ordered him to arrange the funeral. He himself went to report the matter to Jia Zheng, after which the arrangements were put in hand. But money was scarce and every expense was difficult to meet. Remembering all Xifeng’s kindness in former days, he wept more bitterly than ever; and when he saw Qiaojie crying as though she would die, his grief deepened still further. They wept until daybreak, when he immediately sent someone to summon his elder brother-in-law, Wang Ren. Ever since Wang Ziteng’s death, Wang Ren had behaved as he pleased under the indulgence of the ineffectual Wang Zisheng, until he had fallen out with all his relatives. Now, learning that his sister had died, he had no choice but to hurry over and weep for her awhile. Seeing that everything there was being managed on a makeshift basis, he grew displeased and said, “My sister worked herself to the bone managing your household for so many years and never did anything seriously wrong. Your family ought to give her a proper funeral. How is it that even now nothing has been made ready?” Jia Lian had never been on good terms with Wang Ren. Hearing him talk such nonsense and knowing that he understood nothing, Jia Lian paid him little heed. Wang Ren then called his niece Qiaojie over and said, “While your mother was alive, she never handled matters properly. All she knew was how to curry favor with the Old Lady, while scarcely acknowledging any of us from her own family. Niece, you are old enough now. Have you ever seen me take advantage of your family? Now that your mother is dead, you must listen to your uncle in everything. Your only relatives on your mother’s side are myself and your second uncle. I have long known what sort of man your father is: he values outsiders above his own. When that Concubine You died, though I was not in the capital, I heard that he spent a great deal of silver. Yet now that your own mother has died, is he really going to make do with a funeral like this? You had better hurry and speak to your father.” Qiaojie replied, “My father would like nothing better than to make the funeral respectable, but things are not what they used to be. He has no money at hand now, so naturally we must economize in some matters.”

p.src: Wang Ren said, “Surely you are not short of valuables!” Qiaojie replied, “What was confiscated last year has never been returned.” Wang Ren said, “So you say the same thing. I heard that the Old Lady gave you a great many things besides. You ought to bring them out.” Qiaojie could hardly say that her father had used them, so she merely claimed not to know. Wang Ren said, “Oh, I understand. You simply want to keep them for your dowry.” Qiaojie dared not answer him. Choking with anger and unable to speak, she began to cry. Ping’er said angrily, “If Uncle has something to say, wait until our Second Master comes in and speak to him. What can a girl of her age possibly understand?” Wang Ren replied, “You people could hardly wait for Second Mistress to die, so that you might rule the roost yourselves. I want nothing for myself. A respectable funeral would reflect well on you too.” With that, he sat down in a huff. Qiaojie felt deeply aggrieved and thought, “It is not that Father is heartless. While Mother was alive, who knows how many things Uncle took from her? Yet now he speaks as though his hands were perfectly clean.” From then on, she thought much less of her uncle. Little did she know that Wang Ren was thinking, “My sister must have amassed no end of wealth. The household may have been confiscated, but surely there cannot be so little silver left in her rooms. They must fear that I shall pester them, so even the girl joins them in saying this. The wretched little thing is useless too.” From that time onward, Wang Ren too took a dislike to Qiaojie.

p.src: Jia Lian knew nothing of this; he was wholly occupied with raising money for the expenses. He had entrusted the major arrangements outside the household to Lai Da, but a great deal of money was also needed within, and for the moment he truly had no means of raising it. Knowing how anxious he was, Ping’er said to Jia Lian, “Second Master, you must not ruin your health with grief.” Jia Lian replied, “What health? We do not even have money for our daily expenses. How am I to manage this affair? And to make matters worse, that muddleheaded fool is here causing endless trouble. What do you expect me to do?” Ping’er said, “Second Master, there is no need to be so anxious. If you lack ready money, I still have some valuables inside that fortunately escaped confiscation last year. If you need them, take them and pawn them for the expenses.” When Jia Lian heard this, he thought how rare such devotion was and said with a smile, “That would be even better; it would save me from having to seek help everywhere. I shall repay you as soon as I have raised the silver.” Ping’er replied, “What I have was given to me by Mistress herself, so there is no question of repayment. All I want is for her funeral to be conducted respectably.” Jia Lian was sincerely grateful to her. He took Ping’er’s valuables and pawned them for money, and thereafter consulted her about every aspect of the arrangements. Qiutong saw this and felt resentful. She would often remark sarcastically, “Now that Mistress is gone, Ping’er means to take her place. I was given to Second Master by the Old Master. How can she possibly rank above me?” Ping’er saw what was in her mind but simply ignored her. Jia Lian, however, soon understood what was happening and disliked Qiutong all the more. Whenever anything vexed him, he vented his anger on her. When Lady Xing learned of this, she blamed Jia Lian instead. Jia Lian had to swallow his anger. But no more of this.

p.src: To return to Xifeng: after waiting more than ten days, they conducted her funeral procession. Jia Zheng was observing mourning for the old lady and spent all his time in the outer study. By then the literary retainers had gradually all taken their leave; only Cheng Rixing remained, often keeping him company in conversation. The subject arose that the family fortunes were failing: many members of the household had died one after another, while the Elder Master and Master Zhen were both away, and the family's circumstances grew harder by the day. And no one even knows what condition the fields at the eastern estate are in. Things simply cannot go on like this!" Cheng Rixing said, "I have been here for many years, and I know that there is scarcely anyone in this household who does not enrich himself. Year after year they carry the family's wealth into their own homes, so naturally the household is worse off with every passing year. Then there are the expenses of the Elder Master's and Master Zhen's two establishments, debts outside the family, and the heavy losses suffered recently. It will be difficult to expect the authorities to catch the thieves and recover the stolen property. If you wish to put the family affairs in order, venerable sir, you must summon the stewards and send a trusted man to inspect every property. Dismiss those who should go and retain those who should stay; where there is a deficit, make the person responsible repay it. Then you will know precisely where matters stand. No one would dare buy that great garden. Yet it could yield a considerable income, and still no one has been assigned to manage it. That year, while you were away, those people played their tricks with ghosts and spirits until no one dared enter the garden. That was all the servants' doing. The proper course now is to investigate the servants, keep the good ones in service, and drive out the bad." Jia Zheng nodded. "There is something you do not understand, sir. Never mind the servants—even my own nephews cannot be relied upon. If I undertook an investigation, how could I possibly see and learn every detail for myself? Besides, I am in mourning and cannot attend to such matters. I have never paid much attention to household management, so I cannot even tell what is real and what is not." Cheng Rixing said, "You are a man of the greatest benevolence and virtue. In another family with an estate like this, even if poverty overtook them, they would have nothing to fear for five or ten years; merely calling the stewards to account would yield enough. I have even heard that one of your family's servants has become a county magistrate." Jia Zheng said, "If a man begins using his servants' money, the consequences are unthinkable. We can only economize ourselves. As for the properties entered in the registers, all would be well if they truly existed; what I fear is that they exist in name alone." Cheng Rixing said, "Your judgment is entirely correct, venerable sir. That is precisely why I said an investigation was needed!" Jia Zheng said, "You must have heard something, sir." Cheng Rixing replied, "Though I know something of the remarkable tricks those stewards can perform, I dare not speak of them."

p.src: While the two men were talking, a gatekeeper came in to report, "Master Zhen from Jiangnan has arrived." Jia Zheng asked, "What has brought Master Zhen to the capital?" The man replied, "I made inquiries too. They say that by imperial grace he has been restored to office." Jia Zheng said, "That is enough. Invite him in at once." The man went out and ushered the visitor inside. This Master Zhen was Zhen Baoyu's father. His name was Zhen Yingjia and his courtesy name Youzhong. He too was a native of Jinling and descended from a family of distinguished service. His family was related to the Jias, and the two households had always maintained close contact. p.src: Because the imperial deadline was pressing, I traveled ahead day and night, while my family followed at a slower pace. It will still be some time before they reach the capital. I have been commanded to leave the capital and dare not remain long. When my family arrives, they will naturally call at your honored residence, and I shall certainly have my unworthy son pay his respects to you. If he is worthy of your instruction, and should a suitable marriage present itself, I would be grateful if you would keep him in mind." Jia Zheng agreed to each of his requests. After a few more words, Zhen Yingjia rose to leave, saying, "We shall meet again outside the city tomorrow." Seeing that he was pressed for time and unlikely to remain any longer, Jia Zheng had no choice but to escort him out of the study.

p.src: Jia Lian and Baoyu had long been waiting there to see the guest off in their stead, but as Jia Zheng had not summoned them, they dared not enter unbidden. When Zhen Yingjia came out, the two went forward to pay their respects. The moment Yingjia saw Baoyu, he stared in astonishment and thought, “How can this young man look so much like our Baoyu? Only, he is dressed entirely in white mourning clothes.” He then asked, “It has been so long since I last saw my close relations that I no longer recognize you young gentlemen.” Jia Zheng hastily pointed to Jia Lian and said, “This is Lian, the second son of my elder brother She.” Then, pointing to Baoyu, he said, “This is my unworthy second son, named Baoyu.” Yingjia clapped his hands in amazement. “At home I heard that you, my venerable kinsman, had a beloved son born with jade in his mouth, named Baoyu. As he bore the same name as my own son, I found it most extraordinary. Later I reflected that such things often happen and thought no more of it. Who could have imagined that, upon seeing him today, I would find not only his features identical but his bearing the same as well? This is more extraordinary still!” When he asked Baoyu’s age, he learned that Baoyu was a year younger than the young gentleman of his own household. Jia Zheng then mentioned Bao Yong, who had entered Yingjia’s service, and recounted how he had asked about Yingjia’s son bearing the same name as his own. Yingjia’s attention was wholly fixed on Baoyu, and he had no time to inquire whether Bao Yong had been satisfactorily settled; he merely exclaimed again and again, “Truly extraordinary!” He took Baoyu by the hand and treated him with the utmost warmth. But fearing that the Duke of Anguo might depart very soon, and that he must hasten to prepare for the long journey, he reluctantly took his leave and slowly went on his way. Jia Lian and Baoyu escorted him out, and all along the way he continued asking Baoyu many questions. After he had boarded his carriage and departed, Jia Lian and Baoyu returned to Jia Zheng and repeated all that Yingjia had asked them.

p.src: Jia Zheng dismissed them both. Jia Lian went off again to attend to matters and settle the accounts for Xifeng’s funeral. Baoyu returned to his own rooms and told Baochai, “I have often heard of Zhen Baoyu, but though I have longed to meet him, I never could. Today, however, I met his father first. I also heard that Baoyu will arrive in the capital within the next few days and intends to call upon my father. Everyone says that he and I are exactly alike, but I simply do not believe it. If he comes here in a day or two, you should all go and have a look, and see whether he really does resemble me.” Baochai replied, “Really! You grow more careless in your speech every day. How can you talk of some man being exactly like you and then ask us to go and look at him?” Baoyu realized that he had spoken indiscreetly; his face reddened, and he hurried to explain himself. What he said will be revealed in the next chapter.
